subject: Acme POC kickoff - scope, success metrics & next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Mehta <samir.mehta@acme.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 15 Dec 2026 16:03:00 -0800
Subject: Acme POC kickoff - scope, success metrics & next steps

Hi Samir (and Lisa, looped in),

Thanks again for a great discovery call today. As promised, below is a concise recap of the problems you described, what success looks like for the pilot, the proposed scope, and immediate next steps to get the POC kicked off. Please confirm or call out any changes.

1) Key pain points (from our discussion)
- High latency and cost for your current on-prem NLU inference across large query volumes.
- Inconsistent accuracy on short-form support triage prompts (false positives on intent classification).
- Lack of observability into per-request token cost and failure modes.

2) Pilot goals / success metrics
- Latency: P95 generation latency under 350ms for 512-token requests.
- Cost: Reduce per-1k-token inference cost by >=30% vs current baseline.
- Quality: Intent classification F1 improvement >=6 points on the provided prompt set; no more than 3% regression on critical intents.
- Reliability: >=99% uptime during business hours; error rate <0.5% on pilot traffic.

3) Proposed POC scope (4 weeks)
- Model & infra: Host a Redwood-verified quantized model variant in a dedicated pool.
- Workloads: Evaluate on two workloads (support triage short prompts, knowledge-grounded summarization long prompts).
- Eval & prompt set: Run our evaluation harness on your seed prompt set (~500 labeled examples) + 1 week of shadow traffic.
- Observability: Enable per-route latency/cost dashboards and artifacted prompt/eval diffs.

4) Owners / access
- Acme: Samir Mehta (POC sponsor), Lisa Huang (technical lead, will provide prompt set and dataset access).
- Redwood: Marissa Cole (AE, project lead), Rishi Malhotra (Solutions Engineer), Aditya Rao (SRE for Dedicated pool).

5) Timeline (aiming for 4 weeks from kickoff)
- Week 0 (this week): Kickoff call, share access to seed prompt set + baseline metrics.
- Week 1: Private deployment setup, model selection, initial baseline runs.
- Week 2: Run eval harness, iterate on prompts, begin shadow traffic.
- Week 3: Optimization (batching/quantization tweaks), cost/latency tuning.
- Week 4: Final measurements, exec recap, and decision point (expand, extend, or sunset).

6) Access / setup items (actionable)
- Lisa: please share the labeled prompt set (CSV) and a short doc describing critical intents by EOD Thursday. (attachment: acme_poc_promptset_instructions.pdf)
- Samir: confirm whether your traffic can be routed through our staging VPC or whether you prefer we run a secure VPN tunnel.
- Acme security: if you need SOC2 artifacts, we can provide the Redwoods SOC2 packet and an NDA addendum; Rishi can own the handshake.
- Redwood: we will provision a dedicated GPU pool and share access to a GCP/VPC peering request form in the next 48 hours.

Attachments: acme_poc_scope_v1.pdf (scope doc), redwood_poc_checklist.xlsx (kickoff checklist).

Next steps (proposed):
- Samir/Lisa confirm prompt set delivery and networking preference by 12/17.
- We schedule a 30-min kickoff on 12/18 or 12/19 to spin up infra and verify dataset access.

Thanks — excited to get started.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0123

From: Samir Mehta <samir.mehta@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Lisa Huang <lisa.huang@acme.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 16 Dec 2026 08:19:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Acme POC kickoff - scope, success metrics & next steps

Marissa — thanks for the clear recap. Quick confirmations and a couple clarifications below.

- Scope/metrics: Agreed on the proposed success metrics; we will share baseline latency and cost numbers so you can validate the >=30% cost reduction target.
- Prompt set: Lisa will share the CSV and a mapping doc by EOD Thursday (12/17). She may also include a small subset of flagged examples for critical intent review.
- Networking: We prefer a staging VPC peering route (internal policy) rather than a VPN. I'll have our infra team send the peering contact and CIDR ranges early tomorrow.
- Security/compliance: We will require SOC2 Type II and evidence of access controls for the dedicated pool. Please have Rishi send the SOC2 packet and the security checklist.

Also looping in Lisa — Lisa, can you confirm whether the labeled examples include the alt-language variants (EN/ES)? We rely on a small set of Spanish utterances.

On scheduling: 12/18 10:00am PT works for us for a 30-min kickoff.

Thanks,
Samir
Director of AI Platforms | Acme Corp
samir.mehta@acme.com
